course_title: Special Topics in Biology: Machine Learning for Biologist
subject: BIOL
course_description: A course on topics of special biological interest, designed for Biology majors elective credit. This course is repeatable when the topic varies.
course_notes: This course provides an introduction to machine learning concepts and techniques, with a focus on applications in biological data analysis. Using examples from neuroscience, population biology, ecology, biophysics, genomics, and other fields in the life sciences, we will cover key concepts in machine learning, including supervised and unsupervised learning, dimensionality reduction, model selection, deep neural networks. Through a combination of lectures and hands-on exercises involving real-world biological datasets, students will learn how to implement algorithms, interpret their results, and critically assess these methods in the context of biological research. No prior experience with machine learning is required; however, students should have basic coding experience in a programming language (e.g., R/Matlab/python) and knowledge of concepts from calculus.)
